title: Concrete
coreMove: Turn an abstract claim into a shared visible reference people can picture, remember, and use together.
sourcePressure: The source uses Aesops sour grapes, the Nature Conservancy, Jane Elliotts classroom exercise, Velcro Theory of Memory, and coordination language to show how abstract ideas need pictureable hooks.
chapterSpecificMisunderstanding: Adding vivid detail for decoration while leaving the working idea vague.

sourceAnchors.name: Aesops sour grapes
sourceAnchors.detail: the sidecar names Aesops sour grapes as support for a concrete story carrying an abstract lesson across time
sourceAnchors.phrasingHint: Sour grapes lasts because the abstract lesson has teeth, vines, and a fox attached to it.

sourceAnchors.name: The Nature Conservancy
sourceAnchors.detail: the sidecar says the Nature Conservancy contrasts abstract acreage language with more pictureable conservation framing
sourceAnchors.phrasingHint: The Nature Conservancy example turns acreage into something a person can picture protecting.

sourceAnchors.name: Jane Elliott
sourceAnchors.detail: the sidecar says Jane Elliotts classroom exercise made a social dynamic concrete enough to feel instead of merely defining it
sourceAnchors.phrasingHint: Jane Elliotts classroom exercise shows how a social idea changes when students can feel the difference in the room.

sourceAnchors.name: Velcro Theory of Memory
sourceAnchors.detail: the sidecar names Velcro Theory of Memory as support for the claim that ideas with more hooks are easier to retain
sourceAnchors.phrasingHint: Concrete details give memory more hooks, the way Velcro grips because it has many small catches.

hook: an abstract word becomes a physical object every time
counterintuition: concrete is not colorful repeated flatly
examples: museum erosion display repeated from old package

exampleOpeningDiversity.rule: no more than 2 of the 6 examples may open with the pattern 'At HH:MM, <Name> <verb>s'
exampleOpeningDiversity.requiredOpenings: at least 4 distinct opening devices across the 6 examples, drawn from: timestamp+name+action, dialogue first line, sensory detail first, second-person You direct address, retrospective It took her three weeks to see, question-as-hook, environmental detail before any human
exampleOpeningDiversity.rationale: C8 catches Cartesian repetition of phrases but not the deeper template of 'timestamp + named protagonist + prop + decision' that makes 6 examples feel like 1 example with name swaps

exampleSpecs.audience: an operations manager coordinating travelers across languages
exampleSpecs.stakes: missed bags and clogged walkways during a holiday rush
exampleSpecs.requiredBeat: James replaces abstract directional text with a floor decal path that every passenger can point to and follow
exampleSpecs.firstImage: Fluorescent arrows flicker above a carousel packed three people deep

exampleSpecs.audience: a county administrator explaining bandwidth to council members
exampleSpecs.stakes: a grant vote fails if megabits stay invisible
exampleSpecs.requiredBeat: Juliette asks the council to upload the same farm inspection photo on two connections and watches the slow bar teach the difference
exampleSpecs.firstImage: "Tell me when the calf photo finishes uploading," Juliette says

exampleSpecs.audience: a chef teaching new servers cross-contact rules
exampleSpecs.stakes: one vague instruction can send a diner to the hospital
exampleSpecs.requiredBeat: Marco sprinkles flour on a black cutting board and lets servers see the invisible trail become visible under a flashlight
exampleSpecs.firstImage: White flour dust hangs in the prep-room light like smoke

exampleSpecs.audience: an extension officer translating rainfall projections
exampleSpecs.stakes: farmers need to choose drainage upgrades before spring planting
exampleSpecs.requiredBeat: Astrid pours measured water over two soil trays so the runoff shows what the projection means for one field edge
exampleSpecs.firstImage: At 2:05 p.m., Astrid sets two soil trays on the co-op counter

exampleSpecs.audience: a conductor helping beginners feel syncopation
exampleSpecs.stakes: the piece falls apart if the pattern stays verbal
exampleSpecs.requiredBeat: You watch Kiran move the rhythm from notation to claps, steps, and a single tennis ball passed on the offbeat
exampleSpecs.firstImage: You hear twenty bows scrape the same wrong beat again

exampleSpecs.audience: a legal-aid worker explaining rent escrow rights
exampleSpecs.stakes: tenants miss deadlines when the process stays abstract
exampleSpecs.requiredBeat: Marta turns the process into three envelopes on the table and has the tenant place each document where it belongs
exampleSpecs.firstImage: It took Marta two failed clinics to stop saying procedure out loud

skillTargets: convert abstract terms into shared reference points
judge when vivid detail serves or hijacks the lesson
choose concrete anchors that help coordination
diagnose why an audience remembers the image but misses the rule

tryThisNowSpec: Circle the slipperiest noun in your message, then replace it with one object, action, or comparison your audience could point to in the same room.

rhythmVariety.deepReadParagraphLengthMix: at least one paragraph 3 sentences or shorter, at least one paragraph 5+ sentences, at least one one-sentence punch line
rhythmVariety.fullReadInterludeRequirement: at least one paragraph that breaks the scene-then-rule rhythm: a question to the reader, a research aside, a direct second-person passage, or a brief historical reference
rhythmVariety.forbiddenRhythm: every paragraph following the pattern 'concrete anchor sentence -> abstract rule sentence -> elaboration sentence'
